subject: Orbital Commerce security RFI — Hosted API data lifecycle & jurisdiction handling
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena@orbitalcommerce.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jacob Morris <jacob@orbitalcommerce.com>, privacy@orbitalcommerce.com
Date: Wed, 25 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API questions: data jurisdiction, TTL and deletion proof

Hi Sean,

Thanks for onboarding Orbital Commerce to Redwood for our chat/assistant endpoints. Our security team has three follow-ups before we can approve production: jurisdictional handling for requests originating in the EU, canonical retention TTLs (including backups), and the mechanism for providing a record of deletion when a user requests data removal. Can you confirm the following at a high level and attach any supporting artifacts?

1) Can inbound requests be pinned to an EU region so that all transient data stays in EU-hosted clusters?
2) What are default retention windows for request payloads, logs, and aggregated analytics for the hosted API?
3) When data is deleted via API or customer portal, how is deletion propagated to backups and cold snapshots, and what proof can you provide (deletion receipts/audit logs)?

We'd like a short, actionable response we can include in our vendor assessment doc. If possible, attach a concise matrix we can drop into our security questionnaire.

Appreciate it — Elena
Security & Privacy, Orbital Commerce

[Orbital attachment: vendor-vetting-checklist.pdf]

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@orbitalcommerce.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Apr 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API questions: data jurisdiction, TTL and deletion proof

Elena — thanks, and welcome aboard. Quick summary first, then attached artifacts (matrix + short explainer). High level answers below; Marissa and Ben are copied for SOC/ops and billing implications.

1) Region pinning — yes. Customers can specify routing policy at the API key or org level to keep inference and short-term storage in our EU regions (e.g., eu-west-1 or eu-central-1). Requests routed to EU clusters will not be processed outside those clusters except for control-plane metadata (see note).

2) Default retention windows (hosted API) — typical default settings:
   - Request payloads (non-logged mode): ephemeral — retained in memory during inference, not written to disk.
   - Request payloads (logged mode / customer opts in): 30 days by default; configurable down to 0 days for eligible enterprise customers.
   - System logs (operational traces, non-customer PII): 30 days primary, 90 days rolling backups for SRE use.
   - Aggregated analytics/metrics: retained 12 months aggregated; raw per-request metrics 90 days.

3) Deletion propagation & proof — deletion flows depend on where data resides:
   - Live store / logged requests: deletion request triggers immediate removal from primary stores; we record a deletion event in the audit log and issue a deletion receipt (timestamp + uuid).
   - Backups & snapshots: backups are rotated on a 90-day schedule; when a live deletion occurs, we mark the corresponding object tombstoned and ensure it is excluded from restores. For customers requiring shorter backup horizons we offer backup retention contracts and can run an accelerated purge on request (subject to SLA and change window).

Attachments: redwood-data-lifecycle-summary.pdf (one-page overview), orbital-answers-table.csv (fillable), data-retention-matrix.xlsx (matrix keyed to questionnaire items).

I'll let Marissa add the formal language we typically provide in security questionnaires and Ben can confirm options for shortened backup retention in a dedicated addendum.

Cheers,
Sean Gallagher
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
(sean.gallagher@redwood.ai)

[attachment: redwood-data-lifecycle-summary.pdf (1 page)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@orbitalcommerce.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Apr 2028 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API questions: data jurisdiction, TTL and deletion proof

Elena — adding the exact language you can drop into your questionnaire. I've split responses by artifact and included example audit lines you can expect. Also flagged which items require an enterprise addendum.

--- Sample questionnaire responses (paste-ready) ---
1) Data residency and routing
   - "Redwood Inference supports routing by region. Customers may configure their org or API keys to process requests exclusively within EU regions (eu-west-1, eu-central-1). Control-plane metadata used for billing and policy enforcement may cross regional boundaries; customer content remains within the selected region unless explicit cross-region routing is configured."

2) Retention defaults and customization
   - "By default, logged request payloads are retained 30 days. Customers may opt out of logging at the API level or request a different retention term via an enterprise data-retention addendum (example: 7/30/90 day options). Operational logs required for incident response are retained 30 days, with rolling backups retained 90 days for SRE use only."

3) Deletion and evidence of deletion
   - "Deletion initiated via the Customer Portal API returns a deletion_receipt object containing the deleted object ID, timestamp, initiating principal, and a deletion_event_uuid. Audit logs record the deletion event. For backed-up data, backups are on a 90-day rotation; we offer expedited backup purges under a paid SLA and provide a confirmation report for the purge."

--- Example audit log entry (human-readable) ---
Time: 2028-04-26T09:15:22Z
Event: deletion_request_accepted
ObjectID: req_01G9Q2X3Y4Z
Principal: elena@orbitalcommerce.com
Result: primary_store_deleted; tombstone_flagged_for_backup_purge
DeletionReceiptID: del_3b7f2e

Notes / exceptions:
   - Ephemeral inference-only mode: No disk persistence; nothing to delete.
   - Regulatory holds: If a lawful hold is placed, deletion may be delayed and will be communicated through the normal legal process.

Attachments in this thread include the matrix and a short PDF. Ben — can you confirm the mechanics and costs for an accelerated backup purge (we should give Orbital an estimate)?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Product Security (redwood.ai)

[attachment: orbital-answers-table.csv (CSV - 20 rows)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@orbitalcommerce.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean@gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Apr 2028 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API questions: data jurisdiction, TTL and deletion proof

Elena — quick follow-up on accelerated purge and contractual options.

- Standard backup rotation: 90 days.
- Accelerated purge: We offer a one-time accelerated backup purge for hosted customers on enterprise support. Typical lead time 5–7 business days; cost depends on volume and complexity (we price on a per-TB processed basis).
- If you need guaranteed <30-day backup retention we can include that in the contract as a retention SLA (adds to the enterprise addendum).

If Orbital would like, we can schedule a 30 minute technical call next week to walk the security team through the audit log format and demonstrate an example deletion receipt.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
